extracted.intended_audience: Project directors, proposal writers, and project managers preparing invited grant proposals and managing Division of Vocational Education projects (Florida state vocational education institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions for preparing final invited proposals to the Florida Division of Vocational Education and for managing and reporting on awarded projects, including budgets (Schedules I–V), abstracts, narrative assembly, amendments, copyright, final report format, and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: FEIS literature search requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An FEIS search is required for all proposals invited by the Division of Vocational Education; the search should be conducted between the time of invitation and the date of submitting the final proposal and will be the basis of the Review of Literature section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Florida Educators’ Information Service to identify curriculum materials, research reports, journal articles, bibliographies, and program descriptors. FEIS Search Request forms are provided (Appendix A) and contact information is given; include FEIS search results and note years and types of materials searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget categories and narrative consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgets must be submitted on Division-supplied itemization pages (Schedules I–V of DVE form 441) separated into Personnel, Travel, Materials and Supplies, Capital Outlay, and Other Expenses; all items must be related to the project narrative and identifying terms on the budget must be consistent with the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check institutional procedures for assigning items to categories and consult the financial officer for specific guidelines. List items in broad categories to avoid frequent amendments and ensure terms match narrative labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule I — Personnel information and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule I must list all personnel to be paid from the contract by project job title (professional and support staff, consultants, substitute teachers), include months/hours/FTE, annual salary, amount requested from the grant (column 4), employee benefits (column 5), and total cost (column 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List positions by title (not by name) to avoid budget amendments when personnel change. Compute benefits (e.g., fringe percentage) and prorate summer or part-time salaries appropriately. Follow the specified column order and calculations shown in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project director salary limitation and proration
rubrics_metrics.description: The project director may be paid from the contract but the salary cannot exceed the regular salary for the same time period; summer work should be pro‑rated as an appropriate percentage of regular salary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure requested director salary reflects institutional policy; calculate summer compensation proportionally to annual salary and document method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule II — Travel requirements and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule II should cover travel (mileage and per diem at current state/district rates) required by project staff or consultants; in-state travel need not be itemized but anticipated out-of-state travel must be itemized by point of departure and destination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show travel by position title rather than by individual and justify travel in the narrative. Use current state rates for mileage and per diem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule III — Materials and supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule III should list expendable items (office supplies, paper clips, pens), and may include some non-consumable items (e.g., audio-visual materials) depending on institutional procedure; list amounts in broad categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate requirements and group items broadly to prevent budget amendments; confirm with financial officer if non-consumables should instead be listed on Schedule IV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule IV — Capital outlay and equipment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule IV records equipment and capital outlay; specify type and cost of equipment to be purchased, and provide narrative justification. General purpose office equipment is usually ineligible; permanent reference/library books and some A/V materials may be capital outlay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check institutional policy; if equipment is to be rented, show on Schedule V rather than Schedule IV. Provide clear justification in the narrative for any purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule V — Other expenses (communications and support services)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule V includes communications (telephone, postage) and support services such as duplicating and limited printing, testing, statistical analysis (including contracted data-processing), and equipment rental (as opposed to purchase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemize machine or equipment rental here and list support services with justification. Include amounts needed for things like field-testing printing even if final printing is assumed by DVE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget summary and amendment threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for personnel salaries and benefits, amounts should be stated in broad categories; changes of more than 10% in either the personnel or capital outlay categories require a budget amendment approved by the Division of Vocational Education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fine-tuning between categories is acceptable, but monitor personnel and capital outlay changes closely; have financial officer verify figures and schedule assignment. File DVE 430 for amendments when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract format and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is a one-page single-spaced narrative that provides a concise summary and must include: project title; project director; applicant organization with address/phone; beginning and ending dates; total funds requested; objectives (briefly); procedures (brief overall plan); contribution to education (impact/implications); and product(s) to be delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the abstract last even though it appears first in the narrative. Ensure clarity and completeness so the abstract alone conveys scope of project; a sample abstract form is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal physical and typographic specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare proposals on 8½ x 11" white bond paper; duplicated copies of the original are permissible. Type neatly, double-space text, use a left margin of 1½" and other margins at least 1"; use subheadings to organize topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number pages consistently, avoid fancy bindings (a staple in the upper-left corner is sufficient), and ensure tables/charts are numbered and titled and placed near first reference. Appendices should be consecutively numbered with the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular and graphic presentation guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Each table, chart, or graphic should have a number and suitable title and be placed near the first reference. Keep tables/charts/graphs simple and uncluttered; if more detail is needed, reference and place it in the appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide captions and simplicity; avoid clutter; extensive data should be in appendices with references from the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembling the invited proposal — required order and components
rubrics_metrics.description: An invited final proposal consists of (in order): Special Project Request Form (DVE 441) with Budget Pages (Schedules I–V); Abstract; Project Narrative (Problem Statement, Review of Literature, Objectives, Methodology, Participants, Setting, Facilities and Equipment, Supplies and Materials, Staffing, Time Schedule/Timeline, Data Collection and Analysis, Evaluation, Dissemination, Products); and Budget Recapitulation (FA-1/FA 399).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms will be provided by the Division at invitation. Ensure narrative sections follow Book I description and that the budget recapitulation form (FA-1/FA 399) is completed locally as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: General proposal checklist (presentation and completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before final submission, verify the proposal is typed neatly, pages in order with correct numbering, narrative flows logically, table of contents and headings direct readers to important parts, required sections are included (need, objectives, procedures, evaluation, budget), and others have reviewed the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check internal consistency between budget line-items and narrative activities, confirm correct calculations and totals, and consider having one person prepare the proposal for consistent style and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem statement standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The problem should be stated as a problem to be solved or a question to be answered; the proposal must identify and document needs, convince the reviewer of importance, demonstrate value to vocational education (application/implementation), and show usefulness beyond the local scene where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence/documentation of needs and make clear significance; frame the problem so its resolution has demonstrable value to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of literature standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal should demonstrate awareness of similar programs, research findings, and recognized experts; significant related literature should be carefully selected and summarized; ongoing studies included; if no directly related literature exists, indicate most similar studies; relevant projects or pilot studies should be noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include FEIS search results; summarize literature succinctly and relate it to how the current project differs or builds upon previous efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives should be derived from the problem statement, clearly stated, measurable, listed in order of importance or potential contribution, and should tell WHAT will be done. Objectives should include outcome, target audience, completion date, and evaluation method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write objectives that are specific and measurable; include components (outcome, target, date, evaluation) to facilitate assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and activities criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures should describe participants, available facilities, realistic requirements for funds/personnel/supplies, availability of qualified personnel, appropriate sequencing of activities, a realistic timeline, identification of responsibility for each activity by position title, logical relationship of activities to objectives, specified methods for evaluation appropriate to objectives, and a suggested method for disseminating final products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about who (by title) will do each activity, justify resource needs, ensure evaluation methods align with each objective, and include dissemination plans where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results/outcomes expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated results or outcomes should be clearly stated, be a logical outgrowth of objectives and procedures, be likely to solve the identified problem, have their uses anticipated and described, and if a final product will result, the product should be described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how results will be used and who will benefit; tie outcomes to measurable indicators wherever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget review and justification checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure someone knowledgeable about costs and salaries has checked amounts; the budget should be adequate and not overestimated, include fringe benefits for necessary personnel, have justifications for each item available on request, and be reviewed by the budget officer for proper category assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep documentation supporting cost estimates available; be conservative but realistic; consult institutional finance officer before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal submission procedure (invited proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: When final proposal is fully developed and assembled, three copies should be sent to the Division; one copy must have original signatures on DVE 441. All correspondence and the three copies should be sent to the Division (address provided: Mr. Joe D. Mills, Director, Division of Vocational Education, Knott Building, Tallahassee, FL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required signatures are present and that copies are complete and in correct order. Verify address and recipient at time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for completing Schedules I–V (forms guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each schedule includes specific column and content instructions (Schedule I: personnel titles, months/hours, total salary, amount requested, benefits, totals; Schedule II: titles and travel amounts; Schedule III: descriptions and amounts for materials/supplies; Schedule IV: quantity, description, cost for capital outlay; Schedule V: description and amount for other expenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the explicit column instructions on each schedule; use the sample schedules and examples provided in the appendices as models when completing DVE forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright clearance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright clearance involves (1) receiving permission from copyright holders to use/adapt materials, (2) using the correct copyright statement to protect the State product, (3) determining placement of copyright credit lines, and (4) documenting all copyright activities. The project director is responsible for obtaining clearances and for complete documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact FEIS early for management of copyright clearance ('Coping with Copyright: How FEIS Can Help'); document permissions to protect reprinting and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget amendment filing rules and process (DVE 430)
rubrics_metrics.description: File a budget amendment (DVE form 430) when requesting an increase in total funding or when there is a change of more than 10% of funds for personnel or capital outlay. The amendment form must show current totals, increases/decreases, revised totals, and a justification. It must be signed by the project director, agency finance officer, and superintendent/president and sent (two copies, one with original signatures) to the Projects and Grants Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also submit two copies of FA-1/FA 399 Budget Recapitulation/Project Expenditure Report (one with original signature). Subsequent amendments should use revised totals from prior amendments as the present budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-monetary amendment and notification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to non-monetary aspects (replacement/addition of personnel, revision of objectives, extension of project time) require consultation with project monitors and notification to the Division; approval, if granted, will be documented in writing. Submit a memorandum detailing changes and justification to the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate with your project monitor prior to formal notification and keep written documentation of approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final report writing style guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-written final report should use a logical pattern of development, headings as appropriate, topic sentences in paragraphs, illustrations/examples/specific details, short sentences, simple precise words, and avoidance of vague terms, complex phrases, or jargon. Critique rough drafts with colleagues and request informal review by vocational section representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep potential readers in mind—people interested in vocational education who may know little about the specific subject. Use peer critique and monitor collaboration to improve clarity and usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final report structure and content components
rubrics_metrics.description: Final reports typically include preliminary sections, main text (introduction, methodology, findings and analysis, conclusions and recommendations), and supplementary and appendix materials. Content emphasis may vary by project type (exemplary vs. research projects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include methodology and data sections for research projects; for exemplary projects emphasize description of activity/approach and perceived effects. Use appendices for instruments, detailed tables, calculation samples, and other material referenced in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix, glossary, and bibliography standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices should contain detailed supporting materials (course outlines, model schematics, instruments, calculation samples, extensive tables) and be referenced in the text. Glossaries may be included for unfamiliar terms. Bibliographies (if used) should list documents not cited, grouped by type and alphabetized by author with consistent formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference each appendix entry in the main text. Use consistent bibliographic style (examples and references to Turabian or APA given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final report presentation specifications and copy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports should be on 8½ x 11" paper, 16- or 20-pound white bond; covers on light-colored 110-pound index stock with front cover entries in black ink. Prepare 10 copies (one camera-ready unbound for microfiche, the remaining securely fastened — staples or stitches preferred). Use single spacing (double space between paragraphs), type only on one side, keep typed area no larger than 6" x 9" centered, left margin 1½", other margins at least 1", and number pages with specified Roman/Arabic conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use plastic comb bindings; photos/illustrations should be clear with captions; number tables/charts and place as near first reference as practicable; submit one camera-ready unbound copy for microfiche reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final report checklist (quality control before submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submission verify: draft submitted in advance to Chief, Bureau of Research, Dissemination, and Evaluation; cover contains requested information (project number, period, fiscal year); title page completeness; clear table of contents; abstract contains requested info; each section fulfills its purpose; concluding section summarizes accomplishments and significance; recommendations provided; references documented and numbered; supporting materials/statistics in appendices; charts/illustrations identified and related to text; all pages numbered and in order; correct number of copies and correct address; camera-ready copy unbound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the checklist provided in Part IV to ensure Bureau acceptance. Submit draft for review prior to final submission to allow for Bureau edits/requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final report submission timetable and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Final research and research-related reports should be submitted within 15 days from the project termination date; unless otherwise specified, submit 10 copies to the Division of Vocational Education address provided (Mr. Joe D. Mills, Director). One camera-ready copy should be sent unbound for microfiche reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a draft in advance to the Chief, Bureau of Research, Dissemination, and Evaluation; follow the specified copy numbers and mailing instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Products development, review, and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects may result in products (process models, curriculum guides, evaluation instruments, catalogs). The project director is responsible for product development but should submit a draft product in advance to the Chief, Bureau of Research, Dissemination, and Evaluation; final products are due at the same time as the final report and should be submitted separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with project monitors to ensure usefulness and attractiveness; develop a dissemination plan early in project development with Bureau staff assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination responsibilities and expected audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dissemination and Diffusion Section of the Division handles dissemination of project information (may make releases to the Florida Vocational Journal), sends copies of final reports to the U.S. Department of Education and the National Center for Studies in Vocational Research, enters reports in FEIS, and provides microfiche copies. Potential readers include teachers, administrators, and others interested in vocational education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop dissemination plans early; maintain high writing and format standards so reports and products are useful to varied audiences.
